title: Introduce .NET RAG anti-entropy pattern + tool-calling walkthrough and docs site update
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: add a compact, production-minded .NET (C#) quickstart that demonstrates a RAG anti-entropy indexing pattern (background upserts + soft TTLs) and a practical tool-calling federation pattern for external connectors. This fills a gap in our examples library (most samples are TS/Python/Go) and provides enterprise teams with a C# starting point for private deployments.

What this PR includes: a README-driven quickstart, a minimal C# sample app that runs an incremental indexer + HTTP tool shim (dotnet 7), docs site additions (for anti-entropy pattern and tool-calling recommendations), CI workflow to run basic build + smoke e2e, and a short cookbook page with configuration knobs for Dedicated/Private.

Checklist:
- [x] Add examples/dotnet/rag-anti-entropy/ sample and README
- [x] Add docs/rag/anti-entropy-cache.md and docs/rag/tool-calling-dotnet.md
- [x] Update website sidebar and docs index to surface the new cookbook
- [x] Add CI: .github/workflows/dotnet-rag.yml with restore/build/test steps
- [x] Add a small integration smoke test harness that runs locally against a dev sandbox

Notes on design: the anti-entropy pattern in the sample shows a two-process flow: a fast writer that appends to an in-memory delta queue and a background reconciler that compacts and upserts to the vector index (with optimistic concurrency and idempotent upserts). TTLs are soft (application-level checkpointing) so the sample demonstrates how to handle eventual consistency across a Dedicated/Private environment. The tool-calling sample exposes a lightweight HTTP tool shim (auth header + signed webhook example) and a pattern for retry/backoff and schema-validated responses for structured tool outputs.

Related work: Linear ENG-4321 (dotnet examples expansion), DOC-917 (anti-entropy cookbook). Support ticket SUP-1342 reported a partner ask for a .NET quickstart for private deployments.

How to try locally: follow README.md; requires dotnet 7 SDK, running a local dev sandbox via make dev-sandbox (wrapper provided) or pointing to a Redwood hosted dev API key.

Release notes: adds a .NET RAG quickstart and docs; no breaking API changes.
